newsitem.title: USA: Bausch says Q4 to be hit by weak sunglasses.
newsitem.headline: Bausch says Q4 to be hit by weak sunglasses.

text.p: Bausch & Lomb Inc said on Wednesday weakness in its sunglass business would have a larger impact on its fourth quarter than it previously said.
The company, which sells the Ray-Ban brand, said its worldwide eyewear sales were down nine percent from last year's third quarter.

It expects weakness in its sunglass business to continue for the rest of 1996, said William Carpenter, Bausch & Lomb president and chief operating officer. He added the conditions "are likely to have a more significant impact on fourth quarter performance than we announced earlier."
In August the company said it expected its 1996 earnings before one-time charges to be in the range of $2.20-$2.30, below Wall Street consensus at that time of $2.35-$2.40.
Earlier on Wednesday Bausch & Lomb reported third quarter operating earnings of $0.54 a share, down from $0.75 a year ago and below First Call consensus of $0.55.
The company cited "significant declines" in its Ray-Ban products in the United States, despite strong continuing sales of new products, including Orbs and Sidestreet sunglasses.
Sales of the company's thin film, a special coating that absorbs heat or light and is used in light fixtures and eyeware, were "substantially below" last year's figures, Bausch and Lomb said.
It said the thin film business continues to face significant competitive challenges in its overseas markets.

"Clearly, we are disappointed with our sales results in the sunglass business," Carpenter said in the earnings statement. "As we predicted in August, our results were affected by reduced orders by our largest customer in the U.S. sunglass specialty channel."
Sunglass Hut International Inc is the company's largest U.S. sunglass customer, a spokeswoman said. Last week that company said it expected its third quarter results to be below last year's.
Sales of Revo, Killer Loop and Arnette products, as well as key new styles of Ray-Ban, have continued to be "excellent," but have not offset the erosion in sales of older styles, Bausch & Lomb said.
The company cited progress in expanding newer brands, restructuring manufacturing and supply chain capabilities, and in accelerating the development of new products for 1997.
"While these efforts will not affect our performance in 1996, we will begin to see their benefit during the coming year," Carpenter said.

The company said its other core businesses performed well in the third quarter. Its contact lenses and solutions business, in aggregate, grew six percent, and continued to return operating earnings in excess of 20 percent of sales, it said.
